Eco Deco Pet Hospital has been taking care of my Pomeranian, Lucky, for 9 years, and I’m incredibly grateful for the care he’s received over the years. Everyone is always attentive, kind, and genuinely caring.

The girls are bright, friendly, and full of personality, which makes every visit feel welcoming and personal. Natalia and the entire team are amazing, and Dr. Val is exceptional. You can really tell how much they care about the animals and about making pet owners feel comfortable and informed.

After 9 years of bringing Lucky here, I truly trust the team and feel confident that he is always in good hands. I highly recommend Eco Deco Pet Hospital.

Absolute angels on this earth. Dr. Val, Natalia, and the Eco Deco team treated my baby Piper Dream Dobransky and me with such care. I have never met more compassionate individuals. They truly care about the dogs that they are treating.

Dr. Val is honest and compassionate. He won’t lie to you, but he will also listen to you and walk you through very delicate situations while listening to your dog and to you and what’s most important to you both. He’s smart. He knows what he’s talking about clinically, even if it may not always be what you wanted to hear. He’ll hope with you when there’s hope, but he’ll be honest with you when things don’t look so good.

When Piper got very sick, Dr. Val tried countless medications to keep her comfortable—and it worked. We got many good days! We sat on the porch and basked in the sun. We cruised Ocean Drive blasting music so she could smell the ocean. I was even able to wheel her to the ocean to see it one last time on her last day because Dr. Val compassionately medicated her that day.

Whenever I called them about her, they always promptly answered and helped. They saw how desperately I wanted to do right by her—and they walked beside me to help me do so. My baby who went to every day of medical school with me was so sick, and I did not have the expertise to help her, but Dr. Val did. I am thankful for everything Dr. Val did for her.

Eventually, they walked me through the most terrible process you can walk through as a dog owner with a very sick baby that eventually died. But they did everything they could for her. And they were so kind to me during the process.

Piper Dream died in my arms comfortably in her sleep. And while some of that was absolutely luck, the other part was that Dr. Val made sure that she was comfortable enough with palliative medications that her body felt safe enough to let go when it was time.

They have walked me through the aftercare process with such kindness. Especially when I was having a hard time physically letting her go.  It was the hardest thing I have ever had to do in my life. Losing a service dog is like losing an appendage. I will never be able to thank them with the proper words for helping me through that process.

Thank you, Eco Deco team. You did everything that you could for Piper. Piper Dream and I are incredibly grateful. You understood what she meant to me as my service dog. And you treated her with such care.

I got 13 years, 10 months, and 7 days, and her last ones were more comfortable and happy because of you.

We got good time.

Piper and I thank you from the bottom of our hearts.

This doctor killed my kitten.

I found this clinic through a friend and was so excited to bring my very first kitten- a tiny 3-week-old birthday gift. She was incredibly special to us.

At our first visit, they administered the entire dose of flea medication to such a tiny kitten. A few days later, she became very sick. We rushed her back, where they performed numerous tests, assured us everything looked fine, smiled, and sent us home.

Shortly afterward, she passed away.

We only had one week with our sweet baby before losing her. It was heartbreaking.

When we took her to an emergency veterinarian, they immediately recognized the problem. We were told that a kitten that young should not have received that treatment and that, for her age and size, a simple over-the-counter flea shampoo would have been the appropriate and much safer option.

Instead, Eco repeatedly ran expensive tests while our kitten continued to suffer. We spent a significant amount of money from the day we first brought her in until the day she became critically ill. Despite all of that, they sent us home with fleas still crawling all over her body, my lap, and my car. No one properly explained how to care for such a young kitten, discussed pet insurance, or gave us guidance on what to expect or what we should do next.

I truly believe their treatment and lack of proper care cost my princess her life. Everyone who met her fell in love with her, and many people cried when they learned she had died.

No family should have to experience this

She got a little bit better but then 4 days later she was very lethargic again, no drinking, no eating, not getting up. I called Eco Deco Pet hospital and they squeezed me in last minute. Only one day later I saw a massive improvement in my cats well being. 2 days later she is almost like my old cat again, eating , drinking, talking, very affectionate and more energetic . Dr. Val misdiagnosed my dog putting her in further harm and subsequently requiring an emergency visit just hours after my visit to Eco Deco. He refused to admit the misdiagnosis or refund the money that was spent with Eco Deco.

I brought my dog in who was experiencing respiratory distress and cough. He did an x ray, lab work and an exam. He read the x ray and explained that she had pneumonia and sent us home on Antibiotics. Thinking back he never should have sent us home and he should have referred us to emergency care instead of seeing her or treating her due to the state of her respiratory distress.

Just a few hours later she rapidly declined and I rushed her to emergency care. They took one look at her and diagnosed her with congestive heart failure, not PNUEMONIA, with no diagnostics just proper recognition of clinical symptoms (presence of a heart murmur, crackles, respiratory distress, age of the dog). The poor dog spent 16 hours in critical care subsequently.

The following day Dr. Val called to inform me that his radiologist informed him that the Xray read was not pneumonia but instead congestive heart failure as he had read it. I told him that I was already aware of the misdiagnosis. Dr. Val replied "this is not a misdiagnosis, I am a general practitioner who is not trained to treat emergency conditions".

I also happen to work in the medical field and know well enough that a general practitioner should in fact be able to recognize an emergency situation and refer out as needed. Additionally, a general practitioner should be able to recognize the signs and symptoms of congestive heart failure (vs. pneumonia) which is indeed a common diagnosis in aging dogs. He should have also as a GP been able to read his own x-ray correctly between pneumonia and CHF. The misdiagnosis is scary enough but the denial and lack of effort to make it right is alarming.

Steer clear of this practice and Dr. Val if you want safe proper educated care.

It saddens me to leave this review after being a loyal client for over two years, but I feel obligated to share my experience.

In short:
1. They do not take a holistic or personalized approach to treating your pet.
2. They rely too heavily on testing instead of listening and problem-solving. While it’s understood that animals can’t speak, that shouldn’t make extensive testing the default response—especially when owner insight and careful observation can be helpful.
3. Trust your instincts—you know your pet better than they do.

Despite spending over $3,000 on visits, tests, and medications for ongoing issues like vomiting and diarrhea, we rarely got clear answers—almost everything came back negative. It became clear to me that the default solution is always to run more expensive tests, rather than taking a step back and considering the full picture or the owner's input.

The most recent experience was my last straw. I brought my long-haired cat in for persistent diarrhea and suggested it might be due to hair buildup (which I noticed in his stool). They dismissed the idea and pushed for another round of tests—$400 later, still no answers, and the issue resolved on its own and we assumed it was IBS or the hair. Then, when he started vomiting, I called with detailed symptoms asking if it could be a hairball blockage. They offered no real advice and just said to bring him in. At the appointment, we saw a new vet and he immediately quoted me $1,200 in tests. When I asked the nurse if we could start with one, obvious that I was in shock at the price, she was short and said they all test for different things, which was true but the lack of compassions or problem solving for the situation was disheartening. In a panic and not wanting to look like a bad owner, I agreed to do everything. Again, everything came back negative. The new vet suggested it's probably IBS (which has already been discussed with the last vet... do they not have records of the patients and their visits?) To top it off, they recommended a low-fat diet— if the vet knew anything about my cat he would have known that he’s already on a special hydrolyzed protein diet.

We are deeply disappointed with our experience at Eco Deco Pet Hospital. Our dog, Suzy, was initially diagnosed with arthritis through X-rays, and during that visit, the vet found masses on her skin that were of unknown nature (benign or malignant). Instead of taking the time to understand these masses and evaluate their urgency, they immediately scheduled her for surgery to address dental work and tumor removal — all in one long procedure.

Feeling uneasy about the approach, we sought a second opinion, and thank goodness we did. The new vet we visited showed genuine concern for Suzy’s well-being. They thoroughly examined her and emphasized that it was not safe to keep her under anesthesia for such an extended time, especially without fully understanding the nature of the skin masses. Unlike Eco Deco, this vet took a more cautious and caring approach. They used a needle to sample tissue from the masses and examined it under a microscope immediately. Within 20 minutes, they were able to tell us which masses were mast cell tumors that needed removal, while others could be left alone.

Instead of rushing Suzy into surgery for everything at once, this vet recommended addressing the tumor removal first and referred us to an oncologist to ensure her treatment was tailored to her specific needs. They also discussed physical therapy options to help manage her arthritis, showing they cared about her long-term health and quality of life.

This is the kind of care and thoroughness we expected from Eco Deco Pet Hospital but didn’t receive. The stark contrast between the two clinics is appalling. At Eco Deco, it felt like the priority was maximizing profit by scheduling an unnecessarily long surgery and charging for as many procedures as possible. They didn’t take the time to evaluate the masses further or even suggest consulting an oncologist. The new vet, on the other hand, was willing to sacrifice potential profit to prioritize Suzy’s safety and well-being.

We cannot recommend Eco Deco Pet Hospital to anyone who values the health and safety of their pets. It’s clear their focus is on making money rather than doing what’s best for the animals in their care. This experience was a wake-up call, and we are so grateful we trusted our instincts and sought a second opinion. Our pets deserve better than the careless and greedy approach we experienced at Eco Deco.
